name: Cold Hearth

stars.name: Cold Hearth
stars.notes: Millisecond pulsar spinning 214 times per second; its beam axis serves as a sector-wide navigation lighthouse, timed to nanosecond precision.

planets.name: Ashpan
planets.notes: Irradiated slag world that was once the garden colony Hearth; its surface vitrified in the supernova that birthed the pulsar.

planets.name: Cindercroft
planets.notes: Atmosphere-stripped rock where the colony's orbital tether base still orbits as a cold, tumbling ruin.

anomalies.name: The Beacon Corridor
anomalies.location: along the pulsar beam axis, outer system
anomalies.notes: The pulsar's gravity lenses space along its beam into a stable corridor; navigators ride it for pinpoint jumps, making the dead system quietly indispensable to the sector.

asteroid_belts.name: Supernova Debris Ring
asteroid_belts.notes: Heavy-metal fallout from the supernova—gold, platinum, and stranger synthesized isotopes—drifting in lethally radioactive clumps.

stations.name: Ember Watch
stations.location: outer system, above the beam plane
stations.notes: Timing array and memorial station crewed by descendants of the lost Hearth colonists, who maintain the pulsar's official navigation ephemeris.

faction_control.notes: No sovereignty is claimed; the Hearth Descendants' Trust administers Ember Watch under an ancient navigation-services charter that even the Combine has never challenged.

history: Founded around 2100 as the garden colony Hearth, the system was a celebrated homesteading success story until its sun went supernova—an event no model had predicted.
The collapse of 2387 killed the colony in hours; only three ships in orbit escaped, carrying fewer than two hundred survivors who swore never to let the name be forgotten.
In 2412 the survivors' descendants established Ember Watch, converting grief into duty by publishing the pulsar timing data on which every ship in the sector now relies.
description: Cold Hearth is a graveyard that keeps perfect time. All that remains of the star that warmed the garden colony Hearth is a neutron remnant spinning 214 times a second, sweeping twin beams across the dark like a lighthouse with nothing left to warn against. Two scorched worlds and a glittering ring of supernova debris circle it in silence.

Ships do not come here to stay. They come to listen: the pulsar's pulse is the sector's most trusted navigation reference, and the lensed corridor along its beam lets long-haul navigators thread jumps of unusual precision. Ember Watch, crewed by forty volunteers descended from the original colonists, publishes the timing ephemeris free of charge—a condition written into their founding charter and honored by every major power.

Visitors are few but always moved. The Trust permits pilgrims to view Ashpan from a respectful distance, where the old colony's river valleys still show through the glass under searchlight pulses. Some crew members of passing freighters claim that during quiet shifts at Ember Watch you can hear the raw pulsar signal over open speakers—a rhythm so regular it unsettles the mind. The Trust neither confirms nor denies this, noting only that their grandparents heard the same rhythm stop once before, and no instrument since has explained why.
